title: Indian National Arrested by ICE Over False Citizenship Claim to Vote in 2024 Election
excerpt: Mukeshkumar Somabhai Chaudhari is charged in Minnesota with false information in voting and making a false claim of US citizenship, each carrying up to five years. DHS announced the HSI arrest on Friday; an indictment is an allegation, and he is presumed innocent.
body:
• ICE's Homeland Security Investigations has arrested Mukeshkumar Somabhai Chaudhari, an Indian national, over an alleged false claim of US citizenship to vote in the 2024 general election, DHS said on Friday.
  • A federal grand jury in Minnesota indicted him on September 10 on two counts: false information in voting, and making a false claim of citizenship to register to vote or vote.
  • Prosecutors allege he signed Minnesota's voter signature certificate on November 5, 2024, swearing he was a US citizen when he was not; each count carries a maximum of five years in prison.
  • For non-citizen residents, the practical rule is absolute: do not register or vote in US elections — a false citizenship claim can bring criminal charges and deportation, and an indictment is an allegation, not a conviction.

US Immigration and Customs Enforcement's Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) has arrested Mukeshkumar Somabhai Chaudhari, an Indian national, for allegedly making a false claim of United States citizenship in order to vote in the 2024 general election, the Department of Homeland Security said on Friday.

The allegation

A federal grand jury in the District of Minnesota returned a two-count indictment on September 10. According to the Department of Justice, Chaudhari signed the voter signature certificate required by Minnesota law on or about November 5, 2024, in order to vote in the general election. The certificate required him to swear or affirm that he was a citizen of the United States. The indictment alleges he was not a citizen and knowingly made the false statement in order to vote. HSI is investigating the case, with assistance from the Fillmore County Sheriff's Office, and trial attorneys from the Civil Rights Division's Criminal Section are prosecuting.

https://x.com/GuntherEagleman/status/2111130462621954088

"Voting is reserved for U.S. citizens, and falsely claiming citizenship to cast a ballot is a serious crime."

— Travis Pickard, HSI St. Paul Special Agent in Charge

The charges

Chaudhari is charged with one count of false information in voting, under 52 U.S.C. § 21144(b) incorporating 18 U.S.C. § 1015(f), and one count of making a false claim of citizenship in order to register to vote or vote, under 18 U.S.C. § 1015(f). If convicted, he faces a maximum of five years in prison on each count; a federal judge would determine any sentence under the US Sentencing Guidelines. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin said non-citizens who vote will face arrest, criminal charges and deportation. An indictment is merely an allegation, and Chaudhari is presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt.

Why officials are publicizing it

The arrest was announced two and a half weeks before the November 3 midterms, and both agencies framed it as an election-integrity case. Assistant Attorney General Harmeet K. Dhillon of the Civil Rights Division said the Department would hold accountable those who knowingly make false claims of citizenship in order to vote. For the large Indian community in the United States on work, student and family visas, the case is a precise illustration of a line that cannot be crossed inadvertently: eligibility to live, work and pay taxes in the US confers no right to register or vote, and the signature on a voter certificate is itself the act prosecutors charge.
